## Dispatched — R1, `mode:subagent`, one dev in its own worktree

Seat `domain:ui#2`, `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`, at 2026-09-18T23:44Z. Branch `claude/issue-9943-viewtype-totals-page-row-retired`. Declared surface: `packages/plugin-view/src/ViewSwitcher.tsx` + `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`, plus pins and a changeset.

### The repair shape is the whole dispatch, and it is ⛔ NOT objectui#9880's

The dev is told twice, in as many words: objectui#9880's tables partition the **drawable half** and were repaired by deriving the undrawable half (`satisfies` + `Extract`); these three are total over the **whole** `ViewType`, so that shape does not transfer. The prescription is `satisfies Record<string, X>` **plus a separate totality assert** (`Exclude<ViewType, keyof typeof X> extends never`), and the reason is named:

⛔ **without the assert the compiler stops catching an ADDED member — that is objectui#8127's guard and nothing here may drop it.** The pins must hold **both** directions: a retired member no longer produces TS2353 (green), and an added member no table covers still fails (red). A repair that makes `page` inert and silently also stops catching a new member is a regression wearing a fix's clothes.

### What the dev cannot run, said up front

The card's red reading was taken on the spec-main leg through objectui#9860's injection mechanism — which lives in **PR objectui#9877, HELD and unmerged**. ⇒ the dispatch forbids trying to run that gate and forbids reporting its absence as a failure. The type-level property is measured directly instead: the pins ARE the instrument, and both legs are takeable on the installed spec today.

⚠️ And the cascade is fenced in advance: the 5 × TS7016 + 1 × TS7006 that `app-shell` and `example-byo-backend-console` report on the main leg are **cascade** of these three rows, ⛔ not independent defects and ⛔ not this diff's to chase.

### Why this card is dispatchable while the gate is closed

`docs/NORTH-STAR.md` clause 3 bans p2/p3 tool and contract-hygiene dispatches while the product repos hold open P0/P1 — and they do (reading at 2026-09-18T23:44Z: objectui 0/7, objectstack 4/52). This card is taken under the clause's **second half**: 「解锁产品 P0/P1 的仪器卡沿链继承其优先级」. objectui#9860 is `priority:p1`, `pm:blocked`, `Blocked-by: #9943`; this card is the remaining break holding the spec-main shape gate, so finishing it unblocks a P1. The dev is told to carry that sentence into the PR body so the landing seat does not reconstruct it.

⛔ The `priority:p2` label stays exactly as triage set it — inheritance is a **selection** fact, not a re-grade, and this seat neither grades nor routes.

### Premise, re-verified before the claim

All three sites reproduce at the exact lines the card names on `origin/main` `706e09f27` (the card measured `00c4df509`), with the card's own `grid:` control firing 1 and 2 in the same command. Twelve hours and several merges later, unmoved.

Delivery: draft PR, then stop — the seat lands it (the `AGENTS.md:330` conflict is objectstack#19128; the dev acts on the stricter side). No dev-applied label.

## Seat review — ACCEPT

PR objectui#9977, head `4e356208a`, 7 files, reviewed against `origin/main` `feac43909`. NOT GOVERNED (your run, quoted verbatim: `7 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched`). The seat lands it once CI converges.

### ⛔ First, a correction the seat owes YOU

The seat's own check-in note said the verification was 「the three `page:` rows are **gone**」. **That is wrong, and this delivery is right.** The rows must **stay**: the repair moves the **annotation**, so the retired member goes inert at type level while staying live at runtime for the pinned published spec — the same shape objectui#9880 established. The seat wrote that criterion from a model of the fix instead of from the card, which is the same failure class as the seven unmeasured card claims this shift. Corrected here rather than quietly.

### What the seat read itself, at source

```text
ANNOTATION — the thing the repair actually moves
main feac43909  ViewSwitcher.tsx:64    const DEFAULT_VIEW_LABELS: Record<ViewType, string> = {
                ViewSwitcher.tsx:92    const DEFAULT_VIEW_ICONS:  Record<ViewType, LucideIcon> = {
                ObjectView.tsx:1314    const iconMap: Record<ViewType, string> = {
head 4e356208a  ViewSwitcher.tsx:107   } satisfies Record<string, string>;
                ViewSwitcher.tsx:138   } satisfies Record<string, LucideIcon>;
                ObjectView.tsx:1342    } satisfies Record<string, string>;

THE TOTALITY ASSERT — new, and the half that keeps the guard
head  ViewSwitcher.tsx:87    type _AssertNever<T extends never> = T;
      ViewSwitcher.tsx:110   type _UncoveredViewLabel     = _AssertNever<Exclude<ViewType, keyof typeof DEFAULT_VIEW_LABELS>>;
      ViewSwitcher.tsx:141   type _UncoveredViewIcon      = _AssertNever<Exclude<ViewType, keyof typeof DEFAULT_VIEW_ICONS>>;
      ObjectView.tsx:1345-46 type _UncoveredHostViewIcon  = _AssertNever<Exclude<ViewType, keyof typeof iconMap>>;
CONTROL — the same probe on main: 0. The assert is new.

CONTROL — the rows themselves, which MUST NOT move
main: page: 1 in ObjectView.tsx, 2 in ViewSwitcher.tsx   head: 1 and 2 — unmoved
main: grid: 1 in ObjectView.tsx, 2 in ViewSwitcher.tsx   head: 1 and 2 — unmoved
```

Zero `Record<ViewType, …>` annotations survive at head; the two remaining textual hits are docblock prose saying what the shape is **not**.

### ⭐ A1 and A2 together are what make this a repair rather than a silencing

**A1** — delete the totality assert: `TYPECHECK_EXIT=0` and the pin goes red. ⇒ **the compiler catches nothing**, which is precisely why the pin has to exist and why `satisfies Record<string, X>` alone would have been a silent weakening.
**A2** — delete a real row (`chart`): `TS2344: Type chart does not satisfy the constraint never`. ⇒ objectui#5321 / objectui#8127's added-member guard **survives the repair**, which is the clause the dispatch said nothing here may drop.

One leg without the other proves nothing. Both, with predictions declared first, is the whole verification.

### ⭐⭐ And A4 is the leg worth naming: a prediction that came back FALSE, reported as false

You predicted red on reverting `parseMapEntries` to the two-character close search; you observed **green**. Rather than restate the prediction or quietly drop the leg, you measured **why** — the old reader over-reads 392 characters past the literal and no line in that span matches the entry regex, so both readers parse the same 12 keys — concluded the hazard is **latent, not live**, kept the hardening, and rewrote the comment beside it to state the measurement instead of the prediction (`ec37341d9`). ⇒ that comment is now true of the tree rather than true of an expectation, which is the only kind of comment worth shipping.

### The scope increment, accepted

Seven files rather than three, and each addition is forced rather than chosen:
- **`ViewSwitcher.test.tsx`'s `ALL_VIEW_TYPES`** — a fourth instance of the identical defect (`satisfies` over a `ViewType`-keyed `Record` runs the same excess-property check; measured TS2353). Same class, same one-line shape, and the file was already in the diff.
- **`scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs`** and its suite — readers your own diff would have broken: the anchored-map extractor tested `isObjectLiteralExpression` on an initializer a `SatisfiesExpression` now wraps. ⚠️ Touching a **gate's** parser is a widening risk, and the control you lit is the right one: **184 authored names before and after**, so the new unwrap reads the same population and not a larger one. A3 confirms the unwrap is load-bearing (`yielded 0 entries, fewer than the 9` on both anchors without it) and that the two new wrapper cases are not vacuous.

### The published surface did not move, and you proved it

`dist/` byte-identical across the repair — all 13 emitted files equal by sha256, with the base swap proven on disk before its build and the restore proven by an empty `git diff HEAD`. That is why no consumer package owes a test and why the changeset carries an empty frontmatter rather than a patch bump. ⇒ a type-level repair that emits nothing is the cheapest possible landing, and it is measured rather than asserted.

### ⚠️ One thing this card does NOT do, now measured

The refreshed spec-main gate (check run `105804001660`, head `2b3836f07`, 2026-09-19T00:19:51Z) reports **2 diagnostics in 2 files**, and ⛔ **neither is this trio** — they are `normalize-list-view.pageResidual-8429.test.ts:146` (now objectui#9978) and `object-validation-engine.test.ts:162` (now objectui#9979). ⚠️ That is ⛔ not evidence this trio is fine: the same run printed `Tasks: 18 successful, 24 total` failing at `@object-ui/core#type-check`, so **6 tasks never ran** and `plugin-view` may be among them — objectui#9944's lower-bound property, seen from the inside. ⇒ objectui#9860's `Blocked-by:` now names all three, and this card stays on it.

Your three `out_of_scope_findings` are correctly unfiled, and the `plugin-list` one is the right kind of care: you read the alias rather than trusting a matching type name.

## Landed — verified by content on `origin/main`

PR objectui#9977 merged at 2026-09-19T01:14:28Z. Merge commit `8a7e09fa158a01889607b46c855879e99fc29415`; reading taken at 2026-09-19T01:20Z against `origin/main` @ `8a7e09fa1` (freshly fetched).

Verification is by content on both refs, never by sha and never by ancestry. `BEFORE` = `2acd8e109cd3203214c7f9dc917bccfee841ac14` (first parent of the merge commit), `AFTER` = `8a7e09fa1`. Both legs of every row come from one `git grep` pair over the same two paths, `packages/plugin-view/src/ViewSwitcher.tsx` and `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`.

| reading | BEFORE | AFTER |
|---|---|---|
| `Record<ViewType,` as a **type annotation** | 3 (ViewSwitcher :64, :92 · ObjectView :1314) | **0** |
| `} satisfies Record<string, …>;` | 0 | **3** (ViewSwitcher :107, :138 · ObjectView :1342) |
| `_AssertNever<Exclude<ViewType, keyof typeof …>>` | 0 | **3** (ViewSwitcher :110, :141 · ObjectView :1346) |
| ⭐ CONTROL — `page:` rows | ObjectView 1 · ViewSwitcher 2 | ObjectView 1 · ViewSwitcher 2 — **unmoved** |
| CONTROL — `grid:` rows | ObjectView 1 · ViewSwitcher 2 | ObjectView 1 · ViewSwitcher 2 — **unmoved** |

⭐ The `page:` control is the one that matters on this card: the repair moves the **annotation**, ⛔ not the rows. Had the three `page:` entries been deleted to satisfy the old `Record<ViewType, …>` annotation, the type error would also have gone away — and the product would have lost a view. They are all still there on both refs, so the fix is the one the card asked for.

⚠️ One caveat on the first row, stated so nobody re-derives it wrong later. A naive `git grep -c 'Record<ViewType,'` returns **1**, not 0, on `AFTER`. That surviving hit is `ViewSwitcher.tsx:65`, inside a comment: `* ⛔ NOT the annotation \`Record<ViewType, X>\` the three tables in this package`. It is prose the PR itself added to explain the repair, not an annotation. The annotation count is 0; the raw line count is 1. The distinction is the reading — a bare count here would have been a case-artifact-style false negative.

The three tables now publish their own key set through `satisfies Record<string, …>`, and each is paired with an `_AssertNever<Exclude<ViewType, keyof typeof …>>` that fails to compile the moment `ViewType` grows a member the table does not cover. That is the derived direction the card asked for: the tables no longer *claim* totality by annotation, they *prove* it by assertion, and a new view type breaks the build at the table rather than silently rendering nothing.

Closing state: issue auto-closed `completed` by the PR's `Fixes` line. Clearing `pm:dispatched` and the assignee in the same label write; `pm:blocking` comes off with them — #9943 was listed in #9860's `Blocked-by:` line and that edge is now discharged, so the cache no longer has a live reader.
